title: Choose a family code word
detail: Pick a word or phrase that every family member knows, and that a stranger couldn't guess or find online (not a pet's name or a street you lived on). If someone calls claiming to be family in an emergency, ask for the code word.
warning: Don't type your code word on this website or anywhere online. Say it out loud together, and keep it out of texts and emails.

title: Write down your trusted phone numbers
detail: Put these on paper by the phone or on the fridge: the fraud number on the back of each bank card, and two family members or friends you can call to double-check anything. The printable plan has spaces for them.

title: Agree on the "call before you pay" rule
detail: Promise each other: nobody sends money, gift cards, wire transfers, or cryptocurrency because of a phone call, text, email, or online message without first calling someone on the trusted list.

title: Send unknown callers to voicemail
detail: On an iPhone: open Settings, then Phone (on newer iPhones: Settings, Apps, Phone), and turn on "Silence Unknown Callers." On Android: open the Phone app's settings and turn on call screening or spam blocking. Real callers will leave a message.

title: Turn on two-step login for email
detail: Two-step login (also called two-factor) means a thief needs your phone as well as your password. Use the "Lock It Down" guides on this site, and ask a family member to help if you'd like.

title: Freeze your credit
detail: A credit freeze stops anyone from opening new accounts in your name. It's free, and it doesn't affect your credit score. Contact each of the three credit bureaus: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion. You can lift it any time you need to apply for credit.

title: Talk about scams once a month
detail: Pick a regular time, like a Sunday phone call, to share any strange calls or messages. Doing the Scam of the Week together makes it easy. There's no blame: everyone gets these calls.
